title: Ambitious nuclear campus plans show a way forward for the US industry | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Ed Crooks argues multi-reactor nuclear campuses, such as Nuclear Company of America's proposed 6.6GW six-AP1000 Prosperity One in Kentucky and AtkinsRealis/X-energy plans in Indiana, are the right way to cut US nuclear cost overruns, but Wood Mackenzie sees workforce and supply chain as the binding constraint amid a broader construction boom, forecasting grid nuclear capacity of only 111GW by 2040 and 132GW by 2050 (from ~101GW). The newsletter also covers EQT's US$13 billion Range Resources deal and Brent near US$115 amid US-Iran escalation risk.

insights.claim: Nuclear Company of America, a VC-backed firm announced in 2024, proposed Prosperity One in eastern Kentucky: up to six Westinghouse AP1000 reactors totaling about 6.6GW, built in stages starting with two units, targeting construction start in 2028 with no commercial operation date given.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: A large-scale AP1000 order pipeline would benefit Westinghouse and its owners Brookfield and Cameco.
insights.quote: a proposed campus in eastern Kentucky that would hold up to six Westinghouse AP1000 reactors, with a total capacity of about 6.6 gigawatts

insights.claim: Prosperity One has not yet applied to the NRC for licences, entered PJM's interconnection queue, or secured federal financing, and still lacks resolved ownership, investment, power buyers and a grid connection.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Headline gigawatt announcements are far from bankable projects; discount near-term capex implications.

insights.claim: AtkinsRealis signed an MoU with Indiana and Hoosier Energy Rural Electric Cooperative to explore a campus of up to eight Canadian Candu reactors totaling 6GW.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Opens a US market for Candu technology, an alternative to AP1000 for AtkinsRealis.

insights.claim: X-energy is working with Amazon and American Electric Power on a 960MW Indiana project of 12 Xe-100 SMRs, with Amazon pledging to pay the full project cost rather than passing it to other ratepayers.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Hyperscalers absorbing full nuclear costs shifts risk off ratepayers and could become a template that eases regulatory approval.
insights.quote: It also pledged to pay the full cost of the project, and not pass them on to other ratepayers.
insights.locator: Amazon said the project would help

insights.claim: Building multiple units at one site reduces costs because lessons and capabilities transfer between reactors; Vogtle 4 is estimated to have cost about 30% less than Vogtle 3.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Learning-curve economics favor fleet/campus developers over one-off projects, supporting the multi-unit model.
insights.quote: The cost of the Vogtle 4 reactor has been estimated to be about 30% less than the cost of Vogtle 3.
insights.locator: Building multiple units at one site

insights.claim: Vogtle Units 3 and 4 in Georgia, the last new US reactors, were completed seven years late with cost overruns of well over 100%, which has held back nuclear investment.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Execution-risk memory is why financing and federal backstops are decisive for new nuclear.
insights.locator: Investment in nuclear power has been held back

insights.claim: Crooks contrasts China, where People's Liberation Army engineers levelled a mountaintop for four large reactors in a few months, with Europe, where such site-clearing would be unthinkable.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Highlights the structural build-speed advantage China holds in nuclear deployment.
insights.locator: I once spoke to an energy executive

insights.claim: President Trump set a goal of ten new large reactors under construction in the US by 2030.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Policy tailwind underpins the wave of campus announcements.

insights.claim: The administration launched an US$80 billion partnership to build new AP1000s backed by Westinghouse, Brookfield Asset Management and Cameco, and in June committed loans for US$17.5 billion of components for up to ten large reactors, estimating it could accelerate projects by up to three years.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Government-financed long-lead component orders de-risk the supply chain and benefit component makers and Cameco.
insights.locator: The administration has taken a series

insights.claim: If the US is to materially increase nuclear capacity, some of these large-scale campus projects will have to succeed.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Success or failure of the first campuses will set the investability of US large-reactor nuclear.
insights.quote: if the US is to achieve a material increase in its nuclear generation capacity, it will have to get some of these large-scale projects to succeed
insights.locator: But if the US is to achieve

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie says nuclear is more expensive than gas, solar and wind, which will dominate US capacity additions for at least the next ten years, and new reactors cannot play a significant role in meeting the demand surge before the mid-2030s.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Near-term data-center power demand will be met by gas and renewables, not nuclear; nuclear equities price long-dated optionality.
insights.quote: The time taken to develop projects means that new reactors cannot play a significant role in meeting the expected surge in US electricity demand between now and the mid-2030s.

insights.claim: For customers wanting 24/7 zero-carbon baseload, there are few viable alternatives to nuclear and fewer with a proven track record, so the US is likely to add both AP1000s and SMRs.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler clean-firm demand creates a durable niche premium for nuclear despite higher cost.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie forecasts US grid nuclear capacity rising from about 101GW today to 111GW in 2040 and 132GW in 2050, plus behind-the-meter nuclear, especially for data centres, of 11GW in 2040 and 19GW in 2050.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Only ~10GW of grid additions by 2040 is far below announced pipeline, implying most announced projects slip or fail.
insights.quote: We forecast that US nuclear generation capacity on the grid will rise from about 101GW today to 111GW in 2040, and 132GW in 2050.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie expects workforce and supply-chain capacity to be the critical limits on US nuclear growth over the coming decade, with growth potentially accelerating later as those constraints ease.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Back-loaded growth favors investing in nuclear workforce and supply chain enablers ahead of reactor owners.

insights.claim: Accelerating nuclear growth would require making workforce and supply chain capacity an urgent priority for the current or any future pro-nuclear administration.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Watch for federal training and supply-chain funding as leading indicators of a faster nuclear ramp.

insights.claim: The US is expected to add about 160 mmtpa of LNG export capacity over the next decade, 50% more than in the past decade, and 127GW of gas-fired generation from 2026-2036 versus about 70GW in 2016-2026.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Gas infrastructure and turbine demand nearly doubles, competing with nuclear for the same skilled labor and equipment.
insights.quote: the US will add 127GW of gas-fired generation capacity between 2026 and 2036, compared to about 70GW added from 2016 to 2026
insights.locator: The US is in the middle

insights.claim: Data center construction and Elon Musk's planned US$100 billion SpaceX Starbase launch site in Louisiana add further demand for welders and electricians, whose hiring is already difficult and worsening.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Skilled-trade scarcity is a cross-sector cost inflation driver for all US energy and industrial megaprojects.

insights.claim: A US Department of Energy survey found 62% of nuclear-industry manufacturers already report difficulty hiring needed staff.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Labor shortages exist before the build-out starts, flagging schedule and cost risk.
insights.quote: 62% of manufacturers in the nuclear industry were already reporting difficulties in hiring the staff they needed

insights.claim: The National Center for Energy Analytics' middle case requires nuclear employment to rise from about 58,000 today to about 79,000 by 2030, and it is unclear training programmes can deliver the tens of thousands of workers needed for Trump's ten-reactor goal.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: A ~36% workforce increase in four years looks implausible, pointing to likely delays versus the 2030 target.

insights.claim: EQT agreed to buy Range Resources in a US$13 billion deal creating the largest US gas producer, with enterprise value of about $50 billion and more than 9 Bcf/d net production, positioned to serve Appalachian data-centre demand.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Gas producer consolidation is being justified by data-center demand near the basin.
insights.locator: EQT has agreed to buy Range

insights.claim: EQT says the combined company can be free-cash-flow positive below US$2/mmBTU gas and expects about US$20 billion of free cash flow over five years at current futures prices.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Sub-$2 breakeven implies resilience and capital return capacity even in a gas price downturn.
insights.quote: generate positive free cash flow at a gas price below US$2 per million British thermal units

insights.claim: Oil prices reached their highest since May with Brent futures around US$115 per barrel as the US considered escalating attacks on Iran and Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials visited Iran to prevent escalation.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Middle East escalation risk is keeping a large geopolitical premium in crude.
insights.quote: do I make a deal with them, or do I finish them off?

insights.claim: Trump publicly touted that the US is making hundreds of billions of dollars from elevated oil prices caused by the Middle East conflict, while saying prices would come way down.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Signals the administration sees upside for US producers from high prices, reducing urgency to cap them.
insights.quote: Our country is making hundreds of billions of dollars because of what’s happened in the Middle East.
